dialogue.agent:
I understand your concern about the high debt-to-income (DTI) ratio of 49%. A DTI ratio that high does indicate you may face challenges affording the monthly loan payments going forward.

The DTI ratio compares your total monthly debt obligations to your total monthly income. A higher DTI means a larger portion of your income is committed to debt payments, leaving less financial flexibility. Lenders generally prefer to see DTI ratios below 43% to ensure borrowers can comfortably make their payments.

With a 49% DTI, you will have less of your income available for other expenses like utilities, groceries, and discretionary spending. This higher debt load does increase the risk of missed or late payments, and potentially even default, if your financial situation changes or expenses rise unexpectedly.

I would encourage you to carefully review your budget and anticipated expenses to ensure you can manage the monthly mortgage payment along with your other debts. If you have any concerns about affording the loan, I recommend speaking with the lender to discuss your options. Please let me know if you have any other questions.
